task.description:
Revise the three tests that the now-approved §2.5 amendment (lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md) identified as conflicting with the new empty-declared_fields exemption. Read §2.5.4 and §2.5.4.1 IN FULL first -- they name each test, its exact current (now-wrong) assertion, and the specific required fix, with reasoning. Do not deviate from that guidance without a stated reason.

You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed.

Three revisions required (per §2.5.4.1's own preferred fixes):
1. test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs (around line 106-113, the 'with zero declared fields, no suggestion clause is emitted at all' test): revise to assert messages(result) == [] (zero violations) for an empty declared_fields map, since that's now the correct, designed behavior. Rename/reword the test description if 'no suggestion clause is emitted' no longer accurately describes what's being tested (it's now 'empty declared_fields short-circuits to zero violations').
2. test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs (around line 211-231, the AC6 'reverse' test): per §2.5.4.1's preferred fix, use a DIFFERENT before/after pair that never ends in an empty schema -- e.g. seed only 'customer_name' first (so the gateway condition referencing 'amount' is undeclared -> one violation), call activate/2 or validate_definition_graph/2, then ALSO seed 'amount' between calls (schema now has both fields, condition becomes valid), call again, and assert the second call reflects the fresh state (now clean) -- this still proves AC6's re-run-not-cached point (state changed between calls, second call reflects it) without ever passing through an empty-schema state. Preserve the original test's PURPOSE (proving the pass re-runs fresh, not cached) even though the concrete before/after values change.
3. test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs (around line 241-259, 'a declared_fields/condition mismatch reports via the read-only endpoint'): per §2.5.4.1's preferred fix, seed a non-'amount' field first (e.g. 'customer_name') so the demonstrated mismatch stays a genuine violation against a non-empty schema, rather than relying on a completely empty schema.

After revising, also ADD at least one new small test case in test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs that directly and explicitly proves the empty-declared_fields exemption itself: SemanticValidation.validate(graph, %{}) on a graph whose EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY conditions reference several undeclared variables and/or incompatible-looking comparisons returns %{valid: true, violations: []} -- this is now a real, load-bearing behavior of the module and needs its own direct positive-coverage test, not just be inferred from the revision of test 1.

Update test/specs/REQ-372.md to reflect these changes (why each test's expectation changed, and the new empty-schema-exemption test's purpose).

After revising, run the three affected test files in isolation (mix test test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs) to confirm they pass with the current implementation -- quote the real output. Do NOT run the full mix letflow.check.test suite yourself here formally (TEST-RUNNER's job next) but you MAY do so as a sanity check if useful; if you do, report the real numbers.

Claim the handoff (status IN_PROGRESS), revise, then set status COMPLETED with a genuine first-hand result. next_action on PASS: "Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR". Do not touch created_at/started_at. Commit the changed test files, test spec, and handoff, push to origin/feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921. Never push to main, never touch web/.
acceptance_criteria: test 1 revised to assert zero violations for an empty declared_fields map
test 2 (AC6 reverse) revised to use a before/after pair that never enters the empty-schema state, while still proving the re-run-not-cached point
test 3 revised to seed a non-conflicting field first so its mismatch demonstration stays against a non-empty schema
a new direct test proves validate(graph, %{}) == %{valid: true, violations: []} for a graph with multiple undeclared/incompatible references
test/specs/REQ-372.md updated to reflect all these changes
the affected test files pass in isolation, real output quoted
